content:
anna_support: Escalation from customer (reported via ticket INC-8421). Private control plane mTLS handshakes failing intermittently after they rolled a firewall policy update this morning. Errors seen: `handshake_failure`, `decrypt_error`, and occasional TCP RST mid-handshake. Customer says it started ~08:30 UTC and affects all control-plane endpoints.

anna_support: Quick summary of what customer provided:
- pcap shows ClientHello split into two TLS records (first ~200 bytes, second ~600 bytes) and server sends `alert handshake_failure` after second record.
- openssl s_client output shows early EOF/alert.
- They have a corporate NGFW that recently enabled "SSL inspection" policy for egress.

anna_support: attaching snippets they pasted (redacted IPs):
```
# tcpdump -n -r session.pcap -XX dst port 443 and tcp[13]&8==0
15:08:31.123456 IP 10.1.2.3.54321 > 52.14.23.11.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:201, ack 1, win 229, length 200
  0x0000:  16030100c8 010000c4 0303... (ClientHello first fragment)
15:08:31.123789 IP 10.1.2.3.54321 > 52.14.23.11.443: Flags [P.], seq 201:801, ack 1, win 229, length 600
  0x0000:  1603030258 02000254... (ClientHello continuation)
15:08:31.124100 IP 52.14.23.11.443 > 10.1.2.3.54321: Flags [P.], seq 1:54, ack 801, win 300, length 53
  TLS Alert: handshake_failure
```

anna_support: openssl snippet from customer (connect to controlplane fqdn):
```
$ openssl s_client -connect controlplane.redwood.example:443 -servername controlplane.redwood.example -tls1_3 -msg -debug
>>> TLS 1.3, Handshake [length 0137]
    ClientHello, length=311
***failed to create SSL object***
140735...:SSL routines:ssl_choose_client_version:unsupported protocol
write:errno=104
```

sam_eng-sre: Thanks @anna_support. This looks like a classic ClientHello fragmentation/inspection problem. A few follow-ups: 1) Can we confirm if the NGFW is performing TLS reassembly and/or active MITM? 2) Ask customer for MTU/MSS settings and whether TCP segmentation offload (TSO/GSO) was recently toggled on their egress devices. 3) If they can reproduce, ask for a raw pcap and full packet hex of the first 3 packets in the handshake.

maria_eng-security: Also check ALPN/SNI handling by the NGFW. If the appliance terminates TLS and re-initiates to us, ensure it preserves the SNI exactly and forwards full ClientHello. Some appliances truncate or rewrite extensions which breaks TLS 1.3 and keyshare.

anna_support: Customer confirmed NGFW enabled "SSL/TLS Inspection (proxy)" at 08:25 UTC. They say it does MITM with a corporate CA. They provided pcap showing the ClientHello bytes reach the NGFW but the NGFW forwards two separate TLS records to the control plane.

sam_eng-sre: Two practical workarounds we can recommend asap: 1) Ask them to disable SSL inspection for controlplane domains (temporary allowlist) OR 2) If they cannot disable, configure MSS clamping on the NGFW/edge router to avoid client-side segmentation of TLS handshake, or disable TSO/GSO on the host performing NAT. Both reduce the chance of fragmentation.

anna_support: I asked customer to try disabling inspection for `*.redwood-internal` and to test. Ticket note: customer is hesitant to disable globally but agreed to try allowlisting controlplane FQDNs.

infra-bot: NOTE: We saw a small uptick in `handshake_failure` alerts for private controlplane cluster eu-west-1 between 08:30-09:00 UTC. (auto-detected anomaly).

anna_support: Customer tried allowlist for controlplane FQDNs -> initial tests look good (3/3 handshakes successful). They left inspection disabled for those domains and reported reduced errors. However they still see occasional failures ~1/1000 requests.

sam_eng-sre: If intermittent persists after allowlist, suspect NGFW still touching some flows (load-balancer IPs, fallback routes). Next steps: 1) Get full pcap around one failing handshake; 2) confirm if failures correlate with specific client networks/IPs or specific edge proxies; 3) advise enabling capture on NGFW for TLS reassembly logs.

maria_eng-security: From security side: recommend customer rotate any corporate MITM certs used for re-signing to ensure they are in truststores if they must do MITM. But preferred is to bypass MITM for our control plane endpoints. Also escalate to their network/security team to audit the appliance firmware — we've seen bugs where certain firmware versions mishandle TLS 1.3 key_share extension.

anna_support: Customer uploaded a failing pcap. I put it in the ticket. Short excerpt from failing flow shows the NGFW inserting an extra FIN after forwarding the second ClientHello fragment and server closes with alert.

devops_oncall: For short-term mitigation on our side, would it make sense to accept brief out-of-order ClientHello fragments or increase handshake reassembly timeout? That could mask the root cause but reduce customer impact. Thoughts?

sam_eng-sre: We shouldn't change control plane TLS stack behavior for a bug in a customer appliance. It introduces risk. Better to document mitigation (allowlist/MSS clamp) and help customer fix NGFW. If many customers are impacted by the same NGFW vendor/firmware, we can coordinate a vendor advisory.

anna_support: Customer confirms workaround (allowlist) mostly fixed it. They've scheduled a change window to update NGFW firmware next week. I'll keep ticket open and will post any new failing pcaps here. :thumbsup:

maria_eng-security: Thanks all — please add NR to the ticket that this was caused by egress TLS inspection/fragmentation and recommended remediation steps. I'll file a short KB we can reuse for future similar escalations.

anna_support: Closing notes added to INC-8421: reproduction steps, pcap excerpt, recommended mitigation: allowlist controlplane, MSS clamp, disable TSO/GSO, vendor firmware upgrade. Will re-open if customer sees more failures.

sam_eng-sre: 👍
